sketches.title: Laundry Court
sketches.premise: Your appliance has issued an error message, and now a household disaster goes to trial. Both players turn the same boring machine problem into a savage courtroom moment; the judge awards points for how far the argument stretches without losing the machine’s exact failure.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the error’s stated appliance, action, and failure true, even while inventing blame, evidence, motives, and verdicts.
sketches.move_shape: Write one courtroom line—opening, objection, testimony, or verdict—in under 90 characters. Example for “Dishwasher: Drain blocked”: “OBJECTION: The sponge knew exactly where it put the evidence.”

sketches.title: Error Date
sketches.premise: The appliance’s error message is looking for love, and your job is to write the worst possible dating profile for it. Both players answer the same fault; points go to the strangest romantic life built around the problem while the error remains unmistakable.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the named appliance and its exact error true, while adding a believable dating want, red flag, or flirt.
sketches.move_shape: Write a dating-profile line or pickup line under 90 characters. Example for “Oven: Temperature too high”: “Hot, clingy, and one bad date from melting your furniture.”

sketches.title: Home Shopping Fail
sketches.premise: A household appliance error has become a live shopping-channel pitch, with you selling the failure as if it were a miracle product. Both players pitch the same card; the judge rewards the wildest sales promise that never hides what went wrong.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the error’s appliance and failure visible, while presenting it as a product feature, deal, warning, or sales claim.
sketches.move_shape: Write one breathless shopping-channel line under 90 characters. Example for “Toaster: Bread stuck”: “Buy now: the only toaster with a built-in hostage situation!”

sketches.title: Error Prophecy
sketches.premise: The appliance has sent an error message from a future where this tiny fault becomes a legendary event. Both players write the prophecy’s next line, and the judge scores how huge the future gets while the original failure still anchors it.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the card’s appliance and error true as the first cause or visible sign of the prophecy.
sketches.move_shape: Write one prophecy line under 90 characters. Example for “Coffee maker: Water tank empty”: “By dawn, the caffeine-starved kingdom will crown the cat.”

sketches.title: Error Alibi
sketches.premise: The appliance has failed, and someone in the house is already lying about it. Both players supply one alibi for the same error; points go to the most outrageous cover story that still admits the exact fault happened.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the named appliance’s error true while giving a clear, invented reason, suspect, or excuse for it.
sketches.move_shape: Write one alibi under 90 characters. Example for “Vacuum: Brush blocked”: “I was nowhere near the rug; ask the dog and his suspicious lawyer.”

sketches.title: Error Cooking Show
sketches.premise: The appliance error is tonight’s cooking-show challenge, and the host refuses to let a small failure kill the drama. Both players describe the dish, hack, or chef meltdown that comes from the same message; the judge rewards invention without letting the fault vanish.
sketches.criterion: The move must keep the appliance’s stated error true while making it part of a recipe, kitchen instruction, or on-air disaster.
sketches.move_shape: Write one cooking-show line under 90 characters. Example for “Oven: Door open”: “Chef, leave it open—tonight we roast the recipe and the landlord.”
